slot.brief: Figure showing energy level diagram (or Bohr orbit picture) for hydrogen-like species; derive the energy/radius ratio for a transition or compute the wavelength of a transition line.

stem: For the transition shown in the figure, find $(\Delta E_{\text{em}}/13.6\ \text{eV},\ r_4/a_0)$ for $\text{Li}^{2+}$. Use $E_n=-13.6Z^2/n^2$ eV and $r_n=a_0n^2/Z$.

verdicts.working: For Li²⁺, Z=3. The n=4→2 emission has ΔE_em=E₄−E₂=13.6×9(1/4−1/16)=13.6×27/16 eV, and r₄/a₀=4²/3=16/3.

working:
For $\text{Li}^{2+}$, $Z=3$ and the transition is $n=4\to2$.\n$\dfrac{\Delta E_{\text{em}}}{13.6\ \text{eV}}=Z^2\left(\dfrac{1}{2^2}-\dfrac{1}{4^2}\right)=\dfrac{27}{16}$.\n$\dfrac{r_4}{a_0}=\dfrac{4^2}{3}=\dfrac{16}{3}$.

Independent check: For Li²⁺, Z=3. The n=4→2 emission has ΔE_em=E₄−E₂=13.6×9(1/4−1/16)=13.6×27/16 eV, and r₄/a₀=4²/3=16/3.
solution:
For Li$^{2+}$, $Z=3$ and the transition is $n=4\to2$.
$$\frac{\Delta E_{\text{em}}}{13.6\ \text{eV}}=Z^2\left(\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{4^2}\right)=\frac{27}{16}$$
$$\frac{r_4}{a_0}=\frac{4^2}{3}=\frac{16}{3}$$
